docs.text:
• This Repository is my Personal(Now Public) Notebook to take notes on Cyber Security Courses.

docs.text: All information, scripts, and network maps in this repository are for educational purposes only. This playbook documents my learning process in a safe, controlled lab environment. Do not use any of these methodologies against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: 💌 Author's Note
docs.text:
At its core, this repository is simply my daily grind documented. I built this to fuel my passion for CyberSecurity. Whether you are a fellow high schooler trying to learn penetration testing or someone just browsing for a quick terminal command, I hope this playbook helps you on your own journey. Keep learning, keep hacking, && stay safe and stay curious.

Lots of love, Ashu-Cipher ♡

docs.title: Computer Network
docs.text: A Collection Of Computer Devices that are connected in various ways in order to communicate or share resources.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Wired: cables Wireless: Radio waves, IR waves

docs.title: Terms
docs.text: Node/Host: any device on network Data Transfer rate: speed with which data is moved from one place to another on network

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
1. client/server model: provide service
  2. peer to peer model:

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
1. File Server: A computer that stores and manage files for multiple users on a network
  2. Web Server: A computer dedicated to responding to requests for web pages

docs.title: Topology:
docs.text:
• Ring: A config that connects all nodes in a closed loop on which messages travel in one direction.
  • Star: A config that centres around one node to which all others are connected and through which all messages are sent
  • Bus: All nodes are connected to single communication line that carries message in both directions

docs.title: 2. Wide Area Network(WAN)
docs.text: -> Connects two or more LAN * Gateway: one particular node on a LAN setup to handle all communication going between that LAN and other networks. * Internetworking: communication between networks * Internet: WAN covering globe

docs.title: 3. Metropolitan Area Network (MAN)
docs.text: -> communication infra that has been developed in and around large cities

docs.title: Who owns the Internet?
docs.text: -> Nobody. It is made of many smaller network, which are often owned by a person on organization.

docs.title: Internet backbone
docs.text: -> A set of high speed network that carry Internet traffic

docs.title: Internet Service Provider (ISP)
docs.text: -> Company that provide the access of network to other companies or individual

docs.title: Technologies used
docs.text:
• Phone modem: convert computer data to audio signal and transfer using telephone line, modem at destination convert it into data.
  • Digital Subscriber Line(DSL): Uses regular copper phone lines to transfer digital data
  • Cable modem: uses cable TV line

docs.title: Broadband
docs.text: -> Connection in which speed is faster than 128 bps - DSL, cable modem - Speed for download differ from upload

docs.title: HUB
docs.text:
• connect computer together in star topology
  • increases the chance of collision
  • operate in physical layer of OSI model
  • no intelligence
  • flood incoming packet to all ports

docs.title: Repeater
docs.text: -> Regenate weak signals to original level - increase signal range

docs.title: Modem
docs.text:
• convert digital -> sound from sender side
  • sound -> digital on receiver side
  • classified by speed

docs.title: NIC
docs.text: -> Network Interface Card - provide MAC address - hardware to allow computer to communicate on network - OSI layer 1 & 2

docs.title: Switches
docs.text: -> Intelligent HUB - provide traffic control for packets - uses database of MAC addresses to determine location - OSI layer 2

docs.title: Bridge
docs.text: -> Intelligent repeater - uses database of MAC addresses to determine location - database is created dynamically as computers communicate - OSI layer 2

docs.title: Routers
docs.text:
• route info between LANs
  • divide broadcast domain
  • OSI layer 3

docs.title: Gateways
docs.text: -> protocol converters - software in Routers - establish communication between different systems/protocols - can operate at any network layer

docs.title: WAP
docs.text: -> Wireless Access Point - wireless communication device to connect with wireless network - can relay data between wired and wireless devices on network

docs.title: Guided
docs.text: -> Wired Media

docs.title: Twisted Pair Cable
docs.text: -> Pairs of wires twisted - Purpose: cancel out EMI from other pairs and external source

docs.title: TYPES
docs.text:
UTP -> Unshielded Twisted Pair -> Generally best option

STP -> Shielded Twisted Pair -> Extra cancelation

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• cheap
  • easy to work

docs.title: Disadvantage
docs.text:
• Low data rate
  • short range

docs.title: Coaxial Cable
docs.text:
• type of copper cable
  • built with metal shield and other components
  • block signal interference
  • Primary user: cable TV company

docs.title: Advantage
docs.text:
• used in high frequency application
  • improve shield effectiveness
  • high bandwidth
  • cost of cable is less

docs.title: Disadvantage
docs.text:
• bulky, thick, stiff
  • expensive to install
  • security issue
  • grounding necessary

docs.title: Optical Fiber Cable
docs.text: -> transfer data signal in form of light

docs.title: Tyes
docs.text: Single mode fiber (SMF) Multi mode fiber (MMF)

docs.title: Advantage
docs.text:
• Extremely high bandwidth
  • thin, light-weight
  • resistant to EMI
  • long distance
  • low security risk

docs.title: Disadvantages
docs.text:
• cost
  • fragile
  • difficult to install
  • attenuation, dispersion

docs.title: Unguided
docs.text: -> Wireless Media

docs.title: Switching
docs.text: -> mechanism of communication made up ofseries of interconnected nodes called switches. -> uses STAR TOPOLOGY

docs.title: Message Switching
docs.text:
• each message is treated as independent unit
  • each intermediate device store it until next is ready to receive it
  • Store and Forward Switching

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• multiple devices share same channel
  • congestion can be reduced
  • unlimited message length supported

docs.title: Disadvantage
docs.text:
• not compatible for video and audio
  • costly
  • security issue
  • not reliable

docs.title: Circuit Switching
docs.text: -> generally used in public network -> handle voice and digital data -> dedicated link/path established and maintained for entire duration of conversation

docs.title: Advantage
docs.text:
• guranteed data rate
  • no waiting time
  • suitable for long cont transmission

docs.title: Disadvantage
docs.text:
• others can't use same channel
  • more bandwidth required
  • time required for physical link establishment

docs.title: Packet Switching
docs.text: -> data divided into fixed sized packets -> routers direct packets between networks

docs.title: Advantage
docs.text:
• efficient use of network
  • high data transmission
  • no big memory requirred
  • no dedicated path required
  • suitable for video/voice calls
  • less usage cost

docs.title: Disadvantage
docs.text:
• order mismatch
  • transmission delay
  • packet loss
  • implementation cost
  • security issue

docs.title: 6. THE OSI MODEL
docs.text: Open System Interconnection(OSI)

docs.title: Communication Architecture
docs.text:
• strategy for connecting host computer and other equipments
  • defines necessary elements for data communication between devices
  • defines a standard for the communication hosts
  • adds flexibility

docs.title: The OSI Reference Model
docs.text:
• the Primary Architectural model for inter-computer communications.
  • describes how data makes its way from an application programme to another application programme through a network medium
  • divides the problem of moving data into SEVEN smaller and more manageable problems.
  • this separation is known as layering

docs.title: LAYER 7: Application Layer
docs.text:
• top layer
  • provides interface
  • Responsibility: provide service to user

docs.title: LAYER 6: Presentation Layer
docs.text:
• translate data for network communication and vice versa
  • responsible for protocol conversions, encryption/decryption, data compression/decompression
  • redirector operates at this layer

docs.title: LAYER 5: Session Layer
docs.text:
• enable two networked resource to hold ongoing communications across a network
  • exchange of data during that session
  • responsible for initiating, maintaining and terminating sessions
  • responsible for security and access control
  • responsible for synchronization and checkpoint services

docs.title: LAYER 4: Transport Layer
docs.text:
• manages transmission of data across a network
  • manages flow of data between parties by making packets
  • reassemble packets at receiving end
  • provide acknowledgement of successful transmission and request resend for errored packets
  • responsible for delivery from one process to another

docs.title: LAYER 3: Network Layer
docs.text:
• handles addressing and translation for packets
  • decides route transmission between computers
  • handles decision needed to get data from one point to next
  • also handles packet switching and network congestion control

docs.title: LAYER 2: Data Link Layer
docs.text:
• Methodology: 5. DATA LINK LAYER
  • handles packets between Network layer and Physical layer
  • handle conversion of data into raw and vice versa
  • handles framing

docs.title: LAYER 1: Physical Layer
docs.text:
• Devices: 4. PHYSICAL LAYER
  • convert bits into electrical signals and vice versa
  • manages interface & Medium
  • tells software what needs to be sent
  • bottom layer
  • responsible for movement of bits from one hop to next

docs.title: The TCP/IP Model
docs.text:
• used in current Internet
  • concise version of 6. THE OSI MODEL
  • original was defined as four software layers built upon hardware
  • thought as five-layer model

Difference with OSI Model

docs.title: OSI vs TCP/IP
docs.text: OSI TCP/IP 1. generic, protocol independent standard, act as communication gateway between network end and user 1. based on standard protocols, it is a communication protocol, it allow connection of hosts over network 2. transport layer gurantees packet delivery 2. doesn't gurantees packet delivery, still more reliable 3. follow vertical approach 3. follow horizontal approach 4. separate Presentation and Session Layer 4. does't have separate layer for these 5. Transport Layer is connection oriented 5. Transport layer is both connection oriented and connectiom less 6. Network layer is both connection oriented and connection less 6. Connection layer is connection less 7. a reference model 7. implementation of OSI Model 8. doesn't fit protocol 8. can fit protocol 9. protocols are hidden, hence replacable 9. replacing protocol isn't easy 10. protocol independent 10. protocol dependent 11. has 7 layers 11. has 4 layers

docs.title: The Internet Protocol (IP)
docs.text: -> the protocol by which data is sent from one computer to another on the Internet - data is transferred in form of packet via logical network path in an ordered format controlled by the network layer - virtual circuits: the best paths for data travel - Basic Transfer Unit of data: | Datagram header | Datagram data area | - Versions: IPv4 ; IPv6

docs.title: The IP Datagram
docs.text:
• self-contained, independent entity with sufficient information
  • synonymous with "packet"
  • info about destination and interpretation is in header
  • variable in size Packet should be
  • independent of specifics of network
  • independent of specifics of the path
  • understandable to any router along the way or the destination host's IP layer It doesn't handle
  • datagram duplicate
  • delay or out of delivery
  • corruption of data
  • datagram loss

docs.title: Header Format
docs.text:
• gives info about data
  • Version: 4 bit field if IPv4: value= 4; IPv6: value=6
  • Header Length: 4 bit field Help knowing where actual data begins = Header Length field value x 4 bytes Initial 5 rows of IP header are always used Min length(IP Header): 5x4=20 Max length(IP Header): 20+40=60
  • Type of service 8 bit field Used for Quality of Service How the datagram should be used also called Differentiated Service Code Point(DSCP)
  • Total Length 16 bit field Min: 20 bytes Max: max value of 16 bit word = 65535 bytes
  • Identification 16 bit field act as ID all fragmented datagram have same ID
  • DF Bit Do not fragment 0: can be more fragmented 1: can't be more fragmented
  • MF Bit More fragment 0: last or only fragment of that ID 1: more fragment of that ID
  • Fragment Offset 13 bit field position of fragmented datagram in original datagram = no. of data bytes ahead of it in original datagram
  • Time To Live 8 bit field max no of hops a datagram can take to reach destination TTL>=0 at destination: Accepted TTL=0 before destination: Discarded
  • Protocol 8 bit field tells host about protocol used Protocol No.: ICMP: 1 IGMP: 2 TCP: 6 UDP: 17
  • Header Checksum 16 bit field contain checksum value used for error checking
  • Source IP address 32 bit field contains logical address of sender
  • Destination IP address 32 bit field contains logical address of reciever
  • Options 0-40 bit fiels Used for: record route Source routing Padding

docs.title: The fields that may be modified
docs.text:
• TTL
  • Options
  • Datagram Length
  • Header Length
  • Fragment Offset

docs.title: IPv6
docs.text:
• developed by Internet Engineering Task Force(IETF)
  • deal with problem of IPv4 exhaustion
  • 128 bits address having space of 2^128
  • colon-hexa representation is used
  • 8 groups, each group represents 2 Bytes
  • Three addressing methods
  • Unicast: identifies a single network interface. packet is delivered to interface identified by that address
  • Multicast: used by multiple hosts. packet sent to this multicast address is distributed to all interfaces corresponding to that address
  • Anycast: assigned to a group of interfaces. packet sent is delivered to only one meber interface. updates routing tables.
  • Broadcast is not defined in IPv6

docs.title: Header Format
docs.text:
1. Version 4 bits bit sequence: 0110
  2. Traffic Class 8 bit indicate class or priority of IPv6
  3. Flow label 20 bits label packets belonging to same flow help avoiding re-ordering
  4. Payload length 16 bit indicates total size(data+ extension header) if payload length > 65535 bytes, jumbo header is used instead of extension header
  5. Next header 8 bit indicate type of extension header
  6. Hop limit 8 bit analogous to TTL
  7. Source address 16 bytes 128-bit IPv6 address of original source
  8. Destination address 16 bytes IPv6 address of destination next router interface if routing extension header is present
  9. Extension Headers to rectify the limitations of IPv4 Options Field next header field tells about extension header 1 IPv6 may contain 0, 1 or more extension headers but should be present in their recommended order

docs.title: IPv4 vs IPv6
docs.text: BASIS OF COMPARISON IPv4 IPv6 Address Configuration manual and DHCP configuration auto-configuring and renumbering Addressing Scheme Class Division Subnetting Address Space 4.29 x 10^9 3.4 x 10^38 Security Feature dependent on application inbuilt IPSEC Address Length 32 bits 128 bits Address Representation decimal hexadecimal Fragmentation performed by sender and forwarding routers only by sender packet flow identification NA uses flow label field Checksum Available NA Message Transmission Scheme Broadcasting Multicast & Anycast Header length variable, 20-60 bytes 40 bytes Mapping ARP NDP compatibility with mobile network not yes IP to MAC resolution Broadcast ARP Multicast Neighbour Soliciation Best feature NAT direct addressing

docs.title: Information
docs.text: -> meaningful form of data -> processed data

docs.title: Information Security
docs.text:
-> Protecting information from unauthorized access -> Employing tools and policies -> BASIC NEED OF EVERYONE

  • Enigma Machine: used by Germans to encrypt warfare data -> Security is the quality of information -> Security is freedom -> Security is an asset

  • Information in digital system makes Cyber Security

docs.title: Threat:
docs.text: -> a constant danger to an asset -> can be person, object or event -> can be categorized and ranked

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
1. Inadvertent threats: human failure
  2. Physical disasters: natural disasters
  3. Technical failures: hardware or software
  4. Deliberate acts: hacking, espionage

docs.title: Information Security doesn't deal with
docs.text:
• Cyber warfare
  • Information warfare
  • Negative impacts of people on internet
  • IoT security

Solution-> Cyber Security

docs.title: Cyber Security
docs.text: -> Protection of cyber space against cyber threats and cyberspace vulnerabilities -> Deals with deliberate acts -> Doesn't deal with physical and personal security -> Threats via Cyberspace, not threats for Cyberspace

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Confidentiality: No telling to unauthorized parties
  • Integrity: Completeness and accuracy of data
  • Availability: When needed, data is available
  • Non-repudiation: I should accept i sent you the message and you should accept you received it
  • Authenticity: You should actually be who you tell you are

docs.title: Confidentiality
docs.text: -> Roughly but wider than privacy -> Sensitive data should not reach wrong people -> Sensitive data should reach right people

docs.title: Measures

docs.title: 4. General Terminology
docs.text:
• Vulnerability: A weakness that can be exploited
  • Threat: One who exploits a vulnerability
  • Risk: Damage caused by exploiting the vulnerability
  • Asset: Which needs to be accessed after exploiting

  • Bug: Error, fault or flaw in a computer program that may cause unexpected behaviour

  • Impact: The aftereffect of exploiting vulnerabilities

  • Hacker: Gain access with or without malicious intent
  • Cracker: Gain access to damage assets and cause harm, always malicious
  • Infosec: Information Security
  • Penetration Testing: Testing and reporting the security loopholes
  • Vulnerability assessment: Testing and reporting the security loopholes, and telling how to fix them
  • Cyber Espionage: Spying to someone to gain illicit access to confidential information (large institutions)
  • Exploits: Designed to cause unexpected behaviours that an attacker can take advantage of to perform harmful actions
  • Script Kiddie: Newbies/Noobs so called hackers without any skills
  • Zero-day: Vulnerability not known to professionals only to be exploited by hackers

docs.title: Dual Boot
docs.text: -> Splitting your computer's resources between the two operating systems -> Each one will have its own dedicated partition on the same hard drive on the same hard drive or an external drive -> You can't run both OS simultaneously

docs.title: Advantage
docs.text:
• Access to fully dedicated hardware resources like CPU, RAM, etc
  • Perfect for running resource-intensive tasks and programs

docs.title: Disadvantages
docs.text:
• Installation process is complex
  • You have to restart everytime you need to change OS

docs.title: Virtual Machine
docs.text: -> Dedicated virtual environment within your OS allowing you to simultaneously run two or more OS -> Need a virtualization software and ISO file

docs.title: Advantage
docs.text:
• Easy to setup
  • Sandboxed
  • Extra layer of security against malware and security vulnerabilities
  • Can create snapshots of OS
  • Able to move to one computer from another

docs.title: Disadvantage
docs.text:
• No dedicated access of resources between OSes
  • Inconvenient for resource-intensive tasks

You can choose what you want to use, i prefer hybrid method, where Kali Linux is my host OS and you can use custom labs or Machines on Virtual Machine and hack it from your OS

docs.title: Network Configuration
docs.text: • In VM you have 3 different types of Network Configuration

docs.title: 1. NAT (Network Address Translation)
docs.text:
• Just like your home network with a wireless router, the VM will be assigned in a separate subnet.
  • Your VM can access outside network like your host, but no outside access to your VM directly, it's protected.
  • DHCP is internal

docs.title: 2. Bridged
docs.text:
• Your VM will be on same network as your host
  • It can be accessed by all computers as your network
  • DHCP is external

docs.title: 3. Host only
docs.text:
• Host only networking creates a network that is completely contained within the host computer
  • All VMs connected to a host-only network will be visible to the host and to each other

docs.title: LAN Segments
docs.text:
• An internal network which logically divides a private network into network segments, that is completely contained within the Host computer
  • All VMs connected to an internal network will be visible to each other but not to host

docs.title: DVWA
docs.text: -> Damn Vulnerable Web Application -> Download using sudo apt install dvwa -> To start you can run sudo dvwa-start or run dvwa-start from application menu -> Login using default credentials i.e. username: admin & password: password -> You can access it on http://127.0.0.1:42001/ or port no specified during dvwa startup -> Create database on that site -> And you're good to go -> You can stop it using sudo dvwa-stop or run dvwa-stop from application menu

docs.title: bWAPP
docs.text:
-> Buggy Web Application -> Download it from https://sourceforge.net/projects/bwapp/files/bWAPP/ -> Extract it to /var/www/html/ -> Make it executable by running chmod +x /var/www/html/bWAPP -> Install dependency using ```sudo apt update -y && sudo apt install apache2 mysql-server php php-mysql php-gd php-curl -y``` -> Start web server and database server using ```sudo systemctl start apache2 sudo systemctl enable apache2 sudo systemctl start mysql sudo systemctl enable mysql``` -> Go to /var/www/html/bWAPP/admin/ open settings.php change password to "" -> Go to http://localhost/bWAPP/install.php and click on install button -> If you get error then runsudo mysql -u root -pand when prompted to root@localhost password just hit enteruse mysqlthen `CREATE USER 'username'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'password';` and thenGRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON bWAPP.* TO 'username'@'localhost';thenexit

Note: “username and my_password” can be anything you pick/want -> Go back to settings.php and set username and password what you picked -> sudo systemctl restart apache2 && systemctl restart mysql -> Then http://localhost/bWAPP/install.php -> This is such a pain in the ass
